quality_guards: The appropriate stress controls depend on the organisation, job design, workforce, evidence and causes identified by assessment.

Upper-limb-disorder evidence is task- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Occupational-asthma risk depends on the sensitiser, airborne concentration, exposure route and duration, controls and individual susceptibility.
Occupational-asthma evidence is substance-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
Bloodborne-virus transmission risk depends on the virus, source viral load, exposure type and site, and transferred material.
Bloodborne-virus evidence is incident- and exposure-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Livestock risk depends on species, animal behaviour, facilities, handler competence, task and site conditions.
Livestock-handling evidence is animal-, task- and site-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Pesticide controls depend on the authorised product, target, dose, equipment, competence, weather and environmental conditions.
Pesticide evidence is product-, application- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level exposure probability.
Zoonosis risk depends on the organism, animal species, exposure route, activity, hygiene controls and susceptibility.
Zoonosis evidence is organism-, activity- and person-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Tree-work controls depend on the tree, work method, equipment, competence, public access, terrain, weather and emergency arrangements.
